## Jolene

**Identity, relationships, studies/work:** Jolene is an engineering student, balancing classes, exams, projects, an internship (June 2023), and personal growth. She met her boyfriend/partner in college engineering class; they have been together three years as of February 2023, are unmarried, and take the relationship slowly. They game, do yoga, travel, and work on engineering projects together.

**Family, values, goals:** Jolene’s mother died in 2022; her mother taught her perseverance and helping others. A heart-shaped bird pendant, given in Paris in 2010, symbolizes freedom and pursuing goals. Jolene wants engineering to improve communities, especially through sustainable energy, clean water, environmental solutions, affordable emergency technology, and STEM education for disadvantaged children. She values resilience, creativity, service, growth, and appreciating the journey.

**Hobbies, possessions, recurring activities:** Engineering design/programming; robotics; reading (*Sapiens*, Neal Stephenson’s *Avalanche*, self-discovery books); gaming (including *Detroit*, *The Walking Dead*, *It Takes Two*, *Overcooked 2*, *Monster Hunter: World*, *The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild*, *Animal Crossing*, *Battlefield 1*); yoga, meditation, mindfulness, breathing exercises; walks, nature, beaches, lakes, hiking, waterfalls, festivals, scuba diving, and interest in surfing. She enjoys candles, essential oils, calming music (Nils Frahm, Ólafur Arnalds), baking cookies, designing notebooks, plants, and photography. She owns snakes including Susie and Seraphim; Seraphim was acquired in 2022 and Susie around August 2021. She also bought a new aquarium in June 2023.

**Timeline:** Jan 2023—finished an electrical-engineering project; began a major robotics project. Feb—built a sustainable rural water purifier; took a mini-retreat; proposed an engineers-to-children STEM program. Mar—managed study stress with Pomodoro/Eisenhower planning; solved an engineering problem. May—completed a solar-powered vehicle project. June—interned at an engineering firm and practiced yoga atop Mount Talkeetna. Aug—lost project files, began a bullet journal, developed an aerial-surveillance prototype, presented at a virtual conference, and visited Rio. Sept—attended meditation/yoga retreats in Phuket and elsewhere, tried scuba diving, and planned further nature trips.

## Deborah

**Identity, family, relationships, work:** Deborah teaches yoga, meditation, mindfulness, and self-care. She is married and strives to build a loving, open, supportive family like her parents’, whose wedding was in 1993. Her mother died years earlier; her father died suddenly on January 25, 2023. She keeps her mother’s amulet/pendant, visits her old house and meaningful benches, and reconnects through photographs, art, cooking memories, flowers, music, and her mother’s friends.

**Values and goals:** Yoga helped Deborah through a difficult period; she teaches it to give others peace, balance, self-awareness, joy, and community. She values nature, relationships, generosity, reflection, resilience, gratitude, and helping people feel connected. She organizes neighborhood classes, retreats, running groups, gardening classes, cleanups, and community workshops.

**Activities and interests:** Yoga (including Warrior II, Tree, Dancer, chair pose, beach yoga, gentle grounding flows), meditation, mindfulness, running/jogging, biking, walking, gardening, surfing, nature reflection, beaches, forests, lakes, sunsets, music festivals, art shows, reading, cooking memories, detective video games, and community events. She enjoys candles, essential oils, mellow instrumental music, “Savana,” and the album *Sleep*. She dislikes dogs and has cats Luna (shelter-adopted, age five in 2023) and Max (her mother’s cat, age eight in 2023).
